claim: FAK and PYK2 are elevated in adenomas in APCmin/+ mice.
source: FAK and PYK2, elevated in adenomas in APCmin/+ mice and in human colorectal cancer tissues, functioned redundantly to promote the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by phosphorylating GSK3βY216 to reinforce pathway output—β-catenin accumulation and intestinal tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figure 5C showing elevated FAK and PYK2 in APCmin/+ mice.

claim: FAK and PYK2 are elevated in human colorectal cancer tissues.
source: FAK and PYK2, elevated in adenomas in APCmin/+ mice and in human colorectal cancer tissues, functioned redundantly to promote the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by phosphorylating GSK3βY216 to reinforce pathway output—β-catenin accumulation and intestinal tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data on human colorectal cancer tissue microarrays shown in Figure 6.

claim: FAK and PYK2 function redundantly to promote the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by phosphorylating GSK3βY216.
source: FAK and PYK2, elevated in adenomas in APCmin/+ mice and in human colorectal cancer tissues, functioned redundantly to promote the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by phosphorylating GSK3βY216 to reinforce pathway output—β-catenin accumulation and intestinal tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches including knockdown studies in different cell lines (Figure 3D-F) and in vitro kinase assays (Figure 3H).

claim: Phosphorylation of GSK3βY216 by FAK/PYK2 reinforces β-catenin accumulation.
source: FAK and PYK2, elevated in adenomas in APCmin/+ mice and in human colorectal cancer tissues, functioned redundantly to promote the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by phosphorylating GSK3βY216 to reinforce pathway output—β-catenin accumulation and intestinal tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that GSK3βY216F mutant fails to restore β-catenin accumulation while Y216E mutant does (Figure 2A).

claim: Phosphorylation of GSK3βY216 promotes intestinal tumorigenesis.
source: FAK and PYK2, elevated in adenomas in APCmin/+ mice and in human colorectal cancer tissues, functioned redundantly to promote the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by phosphorylating GSK3βY216 to reinforce pathway output—β-catenin accumulation and intestinal tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by xenograft experiments (Figure 2D, 2F) and APCmin/+ mouse studies (Figure 5).

claim: Wnt-induced β-catenin accumulation requires Wnt-induced GSK3β/β-TrCP interaction.
source: We previously showed that Wnt-induced β-catenin accumulation requires Wnt-induced GSK3β/β-TrCP interaction
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Phosphorylation of GSK3βY216 is a molecular determinant of GSK3β recruitment of β-TrCP.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of FAK/PYK2 suppresses adenoma formation in APCmin/+ mice.

evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo experiments using PF-562271 treatment in APCmin/+ mice (Figure 5A, 5B).

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of FAK/PYK2 reduces intestinal levels of phospho-GSK3βY216 in APCmin/+ mice.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of FAK/PYK2 suppressed adenoma formation in APCmin/+ mice accompanied with reduced intestinal levels of phospho-GSK3βY216 and β-catenin
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting data from intestinal tissues (Figure 5D).

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of FAK/PYK2 reduces intestinal levels of β-catenin in APCmin/+ mice.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of FAK/PYK2 suppressed adenoma formation in APCmin/+ mice accompanied with reduced intestinal levels of phospho-GSK3βY216 and β-catenin
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data from intestinal tissues (Figure 5C).

claim: FAK/PYK2/GSK3βY216 axis is critical for the activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in APC driven intestinal tumorigenesis.
source: indicating that FAK/PYK2/GSK3βY216 axis is critical for the activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in APC driven intestinal tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple lines of evidence including in vivo experiments in APCmin/+ mice and human tissue analysis.

claim: Only about 50% of colon carcinoma cells display homogeneous nuclear β-catenin staining.

claim: Nuclear β-catenin staining is a surrogate for Wnt signaling activity.
source: Although APC mutation is believed to activate Wnt signaling constitutively, histopathological studies show that only about 50% colon carcinoma cells display homogeneous nuclear β-catenin staining (Chung et al., 2001), a surrogate for Wnt signaling activity

claim: APC mutation alone is not sufficient to cause persistent or full activation of the Wnt pathway in CRC cells.
source: indicating that APC mutation alone is not sufficient to cause persistent or full activation of the Wnt pathway in CRC cells, therefore Wnt signaling is regulatable in APC-mutated CRCs.

claim: Wnt signaling is regulatable in APC-mutated CRCs.
source: indicating that APC mutation alone is not sufficient to cause persistent or full activation of the Wnt pathway in CRC cells, therefore Wnt signaling is regulatable in APC-mutated CRCs.

claim: The β-catenin destruction complex consists of GSK3, casein kinase 1 (CK1), APC, scaffold protein Axin and β-catenin.
source: A key feature of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway is the tight control of the abundance of transcription co-activator β-catenin by the β-catenin destruction complex, consisting of GSK3, casein kinase 1 (CK1), APC, scaffold protein Axin and β-catenin.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Wnt pathway.

claim: In Wnt-off state, β-catenin is phosphorylated by GSK3 on serine 33 and 37 and threonine 41.
source: In Wnt-off state, the cytosolic level of β-catenin is kept low by its continuous degradation: β-catenin is phosphorylated by GSK3 on serine 33 and 37 and threonine 41, phosphorylation then triggers β-catenin recruitment of ubiquitin E3 β-TrCP (β-transducin repeats-containing proteins), causing its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation (Wu and Pan, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wu and Pan, 2010.

claim: Phosphorylation of β-catenin triggers β-catenin recruitment of ubiquitin E3 β-TrCP.
source: In Wnt-off state, the cytosolic level of β-catenin is kept low by its continuous degradation: β-catenin is phosphorylated by GSK3 on serine 33 and 37 and threonine 41, phosphorylation then triggers β-catenin recruitment of ubiquitin E3 β-TrCP (β-transducin repeats-containing proteins), causing its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation (Wu and Pan, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wu and Pan, 2010.

claim: β-TrCP recruitment to β-catenin causes its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.

evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wu and Pan, 2010.

claim: In Wnt-on state, Wnt ligand forms a complex with the cell-surface receptor Frizzled and LRP5/6.
source: In Wnt-on state, Wnt ligand forms a complex with the cell-surface receptor Frizzled and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein (LRP) 5/6 (Wu and Pan, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wu and Pan, 2010.

claim: Wnt signaling causes stabilization of β-catenin by suppressing phosphorylation of β-catenin.
source: and initiates a series of molecular events ultimately causing stabilization of β-catenin by suppressing phosphorylation of β-catenin (Hernandez et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2013) as well as β-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of β-catenin (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hernandez et al., 2012 and Kim et al., 2013.

claim: Wnt signaling causes stabilization of β-catenin by suppressing β-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of β-catenin.
source: and initiates a series of molecular events ultimately causing stabilization of β-catenin by suppressing phosphorylation of β-catenin (Hernandez et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2013) as well as β-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of β-catenin (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Li et al., 2012.

claim: Stabilized β-catenin enters the nucleus to interact with transcription factors TCF/LEF to activate transcription of Wnt target genes.
source: Newly synthesized β-catenin then accumulates and enters the nucleus to interact with transcription factors TCF (T-cell factor)/LEF (lymphoid enhancing factor) to activate transcription of the Wnt target genes (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Li et al., 2012.

claim: Wnt stimulation induces monoubiquitination of GSK3β by β-TrCP.
source: We previously found that Wnt simulation induces monoubiquitination of GSK3β by β-TrCP, which is required for Wnt-induced inhibition of β-catenin recruitment of β-TrCP and subsequent stabilization of β-catenin (Gao et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Gao et al., 2014).

claim: GSK3β monoubiquitination by β-TrCP is required for Wnt-induced inhibition of β-catenin recruitment of β-TrCP.
source: We previously found that Wnt simulation induces monoubiquitination of GSK3β by β-TrCP, which is required for Wnt-induced inhibition of β-catenin recruitment of β-TrCP and subsequent stabilization of β-catenin (Gao et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Gao et al., 2014).

claim: β-TrCP binds to its substrates through phosphorylated residues in conserved degradation motifs (DpSGxxpS).

evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cardozo and Pagano, 2004.

claim: Tyrosine phosphorylation of substrate is also a recruiter for β-TrCP.
source: β-TrCP binds to its substrates through phosphorylated residues in conserved degradation motifs (DpSGxxpS) (Cardozo and Pagano, 2004), but tyrosine phosphorylation of substrate is also a recruiter for β-TrCP (Sahasrabuddhe et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sahasrabuddhe et al., 2015.

claim: GSK3β is known to be phosphorylated at serine 9, threonine 43, tyrosine 216 and threonine 390.
source: GSK3β is known to be phosphorylated at serine 9, threonine 43, tyrosine 216 and threonine 390 (Gao et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gao et al., 2014.

claim: Mutation of GSK3β S9 to alanine moderately inhibits GSK3β/β-TrCP interaction.

evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Mutation of GSK3β T43 to alanine has no impact on GSK3β affinity for β-TrCP.
source: We found that mutation of S9 to alanine (A) moderately inhibited GSK3β/β-TrCP interaction, whereas mutation of T43 and T390 to alanine had no impact on GSK3β affinity for β-TrCP (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Mutation of GSK3β T390 to alanine has no impact on GSK3β affinity for β-TrCP.

evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Mutation of GSK3β Y216 to phenylalanine almost completely abrogates GSK3β binding to β-TrCP.

claim: Mimicking GSK3βY216 phosphorylation by mutation Y216 to glutamic acid restores the interaction between GSK3β and β-TrCP.
source: Mimicking GSK3βY216 phosphorylation by mutation Y216 to glutamic acid (E) restored the interaction, suggesting that it was phosphorylation that determines the recruitment of β-TrCP to GSK3β.

claim: Mutation of GSK3β Y216 to phenylalanine substantially reduces GSK3β ubiquitination in HEK293T cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mutation of GSK3β Y216 to phenylalanine substantially reduces GSK3β ubiquitination in an in vitro reconstituted system.
source: Consistent with β-TrCP's role in GSK3β monoubiquitination (Gao et al., 2014), mutation of GSK3β Y216 to phenylalanine substantially reduced GSK3β ubiquitination in HEK293T cells (Figure 1B) and in an in vitro reconstituted system (Figure 1C, left panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: In the presence of SCFβ-TrCP1 ubiquitin E3 ligase complex, WT GSK3β and its phosphorylation mimicking mutant Y216E, but not Y216F mutant, are ubiquitinated.

evidence: This is a technical note about antibody specificity.

claim: Loss of GSK3βY216 phosphorylation greatly impairs both basal and Wnt3a-induced GSK3β monoubiquitination.
source: the loss of GSK3βY216 phosphorylation greatly impaired both basal and Wnt3a-induced GSK3β monoubiquitination (Figure 1E).

claim: GSK3βY216F mutant protein interacts with Axin1 as strongly as WT GSK3β in HEK293T cells.

claim: GSK3βY216F and GSK3βY216E phosphorylate β-catenin as efficiently as WT GSK3β in cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Phosphorylation status on Y216 does not affect GSK3β binding affinity for Axin1.

claim: GSK3α and GSK3β are functionally redundant in Wnt signaling.

claim: Loss of both GSK3α/β increases the basal level of β-catenin.

claim: Reconstitution of GSK3β KO/GSK3α KD MEFs with WT HA-GSK3β reduces the basal level of β-catenin to the level comparable to WT MEFs.

evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: GSK3βKKKK15/27/32/36RRRR/Y216E mutant fails to restore Wnt-induced β-catenin stabilization.
source: The fact that GSK3βKKKK15/27/32/36RRRR/Y216E mutant failed to restore Wnt-induced β-catenin stabilization (Figure 2A, lanes 13 and 14) functionally confirmed that Y216 phosphorylation occurs prior to ubiquitination.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Y216 phosphorylation occurs prior to ubiquitination.
source: The fact that GSK3βKKKK15/27/32/36RRRR/Y216E mutant failed to restore Wnt-induced β-catenin stabilization (Figure 2A, lanes 13 and 14) functionally confirmed that Y216 phosphorylation occurs prior to ubiquitination.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that the ubiquitination-deficient mutant with Y216E cannot restore function.

claim: Upon Wnt3a stimulation, β-TrCP recruitment to β-catenin and ubiquitination of phosphorylated β-cateninS33/S37/T41 are substantially increased in GSK3β KO/GSK3α KD MEFs reconstituted with HA-GSK3βY216F.

claim: Phosphorylation of GSK3βY216 is required for the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling by suppressing phosphorylated β-cateninS33/S37/T41 recruitment of β-TrCP.

claim: In SW480 cells, KD of both GSK3α and GSK3β greatly inhibits cell growth in nude mice.

claim: Phosphorylation of GSK3βY216 is functionally important in CRC cells.

claim: In GSK3α/β KD SW480 cells, reconstitution with WT Flag-GSK3α or Flag-GSK3αY279E but not Flag-GSK3αY279F restores in vivo tumor growth.

claim: GSK3αY279 and GSK3βY216 function redundantly in CRC cells.
